site.pageTitle: Molecular Immunology Group — Neutrophils & Innate Immunity

hero.lede: Neutrophils reach an infected tissue within minutes and resolve most microbial encounters before adaptive immunity is ever engaged. Scroll to follow one through its effector programme.

stages.label: 01 / Patrolling
stages.heading: Circulating surveillance
stages.text: Constituting roughly 50-70% of circulating leukocytes in humans, neutrophils are maintained in a quiescent yet primed state, surveying the vasculature with a lifespan measured in hours.

stages.label: 02 / Chemotaxis
stages.heading: Reading the gradient
stages.text: Formylated peptides, C5a and chemokines establish a soluble gradient. Receptor occupancy is translated into polarised actin assembly, which appears to commit the cell to a single leading edge within seconds.

stages.label: 03 / Phagocytosis
stages.heading: Engulfment
stages.text: Opsonised targets are internalised through Fcγ and complement receptors. The nascent phagosome is sealed within approximately one minute and is progressively acidified.

stages.label: 04 / Degranulation
stages.heading: The oxidative burst
stages.text: Assembly of the NADPH oxidase complex on the phagosomal membrane generates superoxide, while azurophilic granules deliver myeloperoxidase and elastase. The response is potent, short-lived, and necessarily contained.

stages.label: 05 / NET formation
stages.heading: Extracellular traps
stages.text: Under defined stimuli, chromatin is decondensed and released as extracellular traps that immobilise pathogens. The same mechanism is implicated in thrombosis and autoimmunity - not a failure of regulation, but regulation operating at the edge of its range.

research.label: Research
research.heading: Innate immunity, resolved at molecular scale.
research.intro: The group examines how neutrophil effector programmes are initiated, amplified and terminated, with particular attention to the point at which a protective response becomes a pathological one. Work combines primary human cells, live imaging and targeted proteomics.

axes.title: Receptor-proximal signalling
axes.text: How ligand occupancy at GPCRs and Fc receptors is converted into the cytoskeletal asymmetry that defines a leading edge.

axes.title: Granule biology
axes.text: Cargo sorting, mobilisation hierarchy and the kinetics of release across azurophilic, specific and gelatinase granule subsets.

axes.title: Phagosomal chemistry
axes.text: Spatial and temporal control of the oxidative burst, and the mechanisms limiting collateral damage to surrounding tissue.

axes.title: NETs in disease
axes.text: Contribution of extracellular traps to immunothrombosis, autoantibody generation and chronic inflammatory pathology.

methods.label: Methods
methods.heading: A deliberately narrow toolkit, applied carefully.
methods.intro: Primary human neutrophils are short-lived and readily activated by handling; every assay in the group is benchmarked against an unstimulated control drawn from the same donor within the same hour.

quote.text: The neutrophil is often described as a blunt instrument. The evidence suggests the opposite: a cell capable of graded, reversible and spatially confined decisions, which happens to be committed to them irreversibly.
